name: com.tickerdb/mcp-server
title: TickerDB
description: Point-in-time market data for AI agents: stocks, ETFs and crypto as named bands plus raw values.

tools.name: get_schema
tools.description: Look up field names, descriptions, units and band values. Search rather than pulling everything (~400 KB): search="bull flag", category=patterns, level=market. Names are <group>_<name>[_<unit>]; bands end in a category word (_zone, _state, _trend), raw numbers in a unit (_pct, _ratio, _usd). SEC statement ratios: category=fundamentals. Every band (tracked: true) also has _prev, _periods, _flips_recent_count, _flips_lookback and _stability, usable as fields and filters; lookups omit those rows unless markers=true. Over 25 matches lists names only: search again by exact name for a description.

search.description: Words that must all appear in name, category or description.

level.description: ticker = per-asset fields; market = market_*/macro_*; model = model_* (TickerDB's trading models); statement = financial-statement lines (get_statements).

compact.description: Name, type, values and description only.

store_as.description: Table name: store rows in SQLite, return only a summary. Read with query_data.

append.description: Add rows to an existing store_as table instead of replacing it.

tools.name: query
tools.description: Any cross-section or history (one ticker's full snapshot: get_summary). Give fields and filters (names from get_schema, e.g. fundamentals_returns_zone in [high, very_high]), then EITHER date (default latest) OR start+end. One date with filters, tickers, sort_by or limit: a ranked screen. One date with only fields: every asset. A range: every row in it, weekly by default past ~6 months; market_/macro_ filters keep only dates in that regime, other filters apply after the rows are fetched, so narrow with tickers, member_of or asset_class. Big pulls: store_as + fetch_all, then query_data.

fields.description: Columns, e.g. ["market_cap_usd","momentum_rsi_zone"]. Max 30. On a daily range, statement lines too as statement.<line> (e.g. statement.revenue; get_schema level=statement).

filters.description: Up to 10; a row must match all of them. A null value matches none, but eq/neq null finds missing/present values. E.g. [{"field":"momentum_rsi_zone","op":"in","value":["oversold"]}]. As-filed fundamentals only: fundamentals_statement_source eq "sec".

timeframe.description: Default: weekly for ranges over ~6 months, else daily.

asset_class.description: Only this asset class (etf includes ETNs).

member_of.description: Only members of this index on the row's date, e.g. sp500. Ids: get_indexes.

held_by.description: Only assets this fund held on the row's date: fund ticker (IVV) or SEC series id.

sort_by.description: Ticker field to rank by (one date).

limit.description: Rows on one date (default 20, max 250); rows per page on a range.

offset.description: One date: skip this many ranked rows.

page_token.description: Range: a token from page_tokens or next_page_token (same params).

dry_run.description: Range without a market_/macro_ filter: returns what it would cost in credits. No data, no charge.

adjustment.description: With ohlcv: split (default), split_dividend (total return) or raw (as traded).

store_as.description: Table name: store rows in SQLite, return only a summary. Read with query_data.

append.description: Add rows to an existing store_as table instead of replacing it.

fetch_all.description: Follow every page into store_as in this one call.

tools.name: get_summary
tools.description: One ticker's state: latest snapshot, one date, a start/end series (up to 50 rows; for a longer range add sample=even or use query), or band events. For events give field and optionally band: each says when the band was entered, what it left and how long that had lasted; stats=true returns how often each band was entered. fields trims to sections, paths or field names, e.g. trend, momentum.rsi_zone, fundamentals_pe_ratio. Field names are the get_schema names everywhere (no aliases). Market regimes are in get_market.

fields.description: Sections, dotted paths, or get_schema field names.

meta.description: Add stability metadata (_meta) to every band.

field.description: Band field for events, e.g. momentum_rsi_zone.

band.description: Only changes into this value, e.g. oversold.

sample.description: Up to 50 rows spread evenly across start/end.

stats.description: How often each band was entered, instead of the event list.

context_ticker.description: Keep only events when this second asset was in context_band, e.g. SPY. Needs context_field and context_band.

adjustment.description: Price basis: split (default), split_dividend (total return) or raw (as traded).

store_as.description: Table name: store rows in SQLite, return only a summary. Read with query_data.

append.description: Add rows to an existing store_as table instead of replacing it.

tools.name: get_market
tools.description: Market-level rows, one per date, point in time: US equity market regime (market_*) and economy (macro_*) bands and values, e.g. market_regime_zone, macro_yield_curve_zone. changes=true returns only dates where a band changed. Field list: get_schema level=market. To find tickers under a regime, put market_/macro_ filters into query.

fields.description: JSON array of market fields; ["*"] adds change markers.

filters.description: JSON array of {field, op, value} on market fields.

changes.description: true: only dates where any band changed. Or a JSON array of the bands to watch.

tools.description: End-of-day OHLCV candles for one ticker, daily or weekly (weeks dated by Sunday). Paged: pass next_cursor back as cursor, or use store_as with fetch_all for the whole range in one call.

adjustment.description: split (default), split_dividend (total return) or raw (as traded).

tools.name: add_watchlist_tickers
tools.description: Add tickers to the user's TickerDB watchlist (one per account, shared with the website's Track buttons and Claude/ChatGPT watchlist links). Idempotent: already-present tickers come back in already; unknown ones in unknown. No ticker limit; free. Then get_watchlist_diff (call_tool) reports what changed for them since the last check: score, upside and downside potential, earnings, big price moves, trend changes, RSI oversold, volume spikes, insider trades, analyst changes, serious 8-K filings and dividend cuts.

tools.name: remove_watchlist_tickers
tools.description: Remove tickers from the user's TickerDB watchlist. Idempotent: tickers not on it come back in missing. Free.

tools.name: search_tools
tools.description: Find the other TickerDB endpoints: diff (what changed for your tickers), the watchlist and what changed for it, financial statements (income, balance sheet, cash flow; point in time), insiders, insider trades and holdings, funds, fund holdings and holders, indexes, index members, TickerDB's trading models (list, detail, history, holdings, trades; Pro and Commercial plans, except a model's newest holdings, on every plan), status, account, and the raw search and universe routes. Returns each match's name, purpose and params (* = required). Empty query lists all. Run one with call_tool.

tools.name: call_tool
tools.description: Run an endpoint found with search_tools: its name plus a params object. store_as, append and fetch_all work as on the other data tools.

tools.name: query_data
tools.description: Read-only SQL (SQLite) over tables saved with store_as: SELECT or WITH, plus SHOW TABLES and DESCRIBE <table>. Returns at most 200 rows. Nested fields are flattened with _ (trend.direction -> trend_direction); booleans are 1/0. Tables are kept per API key and deleted 24 h after last use; format=csv returns CSV text.

format.description: csv: rows as CSV text. Default json.
